introHtml:

If your roofer is already on site for a detach and reset, we'll fold the hail inspection into the same visit. Call (970) 286-3417 for a free written estimate.

sections.heading: Weld County Is America's Hail Capital, and Your Panels Sit Right in the Middle of It
sections.html:
Weld County gets hit by hail more often than any other county in the United States. That's not local bragging, it's insurance industry data, and it's why Greeley homeowners see roof claims as a routine part of owning a house here. Your solar array sits on the most exposed surface of your property, angled toward the sky, and it takes the same beating your shingles do.

Most panels are rated to survive 1-inch hail at around 50 mph. The storms that roll off the Front Range regularly drop stones bigger than that, and even hail that doesn't shatter the glass can transfer enough impact energy to crack the silicon cells underneath. That's why a panel that looks fine from the ground can still be a legitimate claim item.

If a storm just came through and you're not sure what you're looking at, don't get on the roof. Call (970) 286-3417 and we'll take a look. Inspections are free, and if the array is genuinely fine, we'll tell you that in writing too.

sections.heading: Shattered Glass vs. Invisible Microcracks: What We Actually Check
sections.html:
Hail damage on solar panels shows up in two forms. The first is the obvious kind: spidered or shattered tempered glass, dented frames, cracked junction boxes, and torn wiring. The second is microcracking, where the impact fractures the solar cells beneath intact glass. Microcracks spread over time with every freeze-thaw cycle and every hot afternoon, and they quietly drag your production down month after month.

Our inspection covers both. Here's what a full workup includes:

  • Panel-by-panel visual inspection of glass, frames, backsheets, and mounting hardware
  • Production-drop diagnosis comparing your monitoring data before and after the storm date
  • String and panel-level electrical testing to isolate which units are underperforming
  • Inverter and optimizer checks, since power surges during storms take out electronics too
  • Racking and roof penetration review, especially important if a reroof is coming

A measurable production drop tied to a documented storm date is often the strongest evidence in a hail claim. If your app shows output falling 10 to 30 percent since the storm and nothing else changed, that's not a coincidence, and we'll put the numbers in your report.

sections.heading: Documentation Your Insurance Adjuster Will Actually Accept
sections.html:
Here's the frustrating truth about solar hail claims: adjusters see a lot of them, and vague claims get denied. "The panels look damaged" doesn't move a claim. What moves a claim is specific, dated, technical documentation from a company that works on solar equipment for a living. That's what we build for you.

Our reports include time-stamped photos of each affected panel, serial numbers, model specs, electrical test results, a production comparison from your monitoring platform, and line-item replacement costs. We format it so the adjuster can lift our numbers directly into the claim scope. When the carrier sends out their own inspector, we're happy to meet them on the roof and walk the array together.

We're not public adjusters and we don't negotiate your claim for you. What we do is make sure the physical evidence and the pricing are solid enough that there's not much left to argue about. Most Greeley homeowners we work with see solar line items approved in the same claim as the roof.

sections.heading: Repair, Replacement, and Working With Your Roofer's Scope
sections.html:
Once the claim is approved, we handle the fix. For cracked or shattered panels, that means sourcing matching or electrically compatible replacements, swapping the damaged units, and re-commissioning the system. Discontinued panel models are common on arrays more than a few years old, and we know which current panels can legally and safely mix into an existing string. Storm-damaged inverters and optimizers get replaced at the same time so you're not chasing a second failure in six months.

Most hail claims in Greeley include a roof replacement, which means your panels need to come off anyway. If that's your situation, the smart move is bundling the hail repair with the detach and reset: we remove the array, your roofer replaces the roof, and we reinstall with the damaged panels swapped out in one mobilization instead of two. That saves you a second round of labor, and the detach and reset line item usually belongs in the roof scope. Our cost guide breaks down what those numbers should look like.

If a panel is beyond saving and you'd rather downsize the array or remove it entirely, we do straight solar panel removal too. Either way, you get a free written estimate before any work starts, and we serve the whole area, from Greeley and Evans out to Windsor and Eaton.

faq.q: Can hail really break solar panels?
faq.a: Yes. Most residential panels are tested to withstand 1-inch hail at roughly 50 mph, but Weld County storms regularly drop stones 1.5 to 2.5 inches across at higher speeds. Direct hits can shatter the tempered glass outright, and even sub-1-inch hail in volume can cause cell microcracks under glass that looks untouched.

faq.q: My panels look fine but my production dropped after the storm. What's going on?
faq.a: That pattern points to microcracks in the cells, which don't show on the surface. We routinely see post-hail production drops of 10 to 30 percent on arrays with zero visible glass damage. We pull your monitoring history, compare output before and after the storm date while adjusting for weather, and run electrical tests to identify which panels are underperforming. That comparison becomes core evidence for your claim.

faq.q: How much does it cost to replace hail-damaged solar panels?
faq.a: A typical residential panel runs $250 to $450 for the hardware, plus labor, so a single swap usually lands between $400 and $700 installed. Replacing a storm-damaged string inverter runs about $1,500 to $3,000 installed, and individual optimizers or microinverters run $150 to $350 each. If insurance approves the claim, these costs come out of the settlement, not your pocket, minus your deductible.

faq.q: Will my homeowners insurance cover solar hail damage?
faq.a: In most cases yes, because rooftop panels attached to your home are typically covered under the dwelling portion of a standard policy, the same coverage paying for your roof. The catch is documentation. Carriers want dated proof tying the damage to a specific storm, which is exactly what our inspection report provides. File within your policy's claim window, usually 365 days from the storm date in Colorado, and get the inspection done early.

faq.q: My roof is being replaced under the same claim. Should the panels come off first?
faq.a: Yes, panels have to come off for a proper reroof, and the detach and reset should be a line item in the roof scope. Plan on roughly $150 to $300 per panel for the full remove-and-reinstall, so a 20-panel array typically runs $3,000 to $6,000. If some panels are hail-damaged, we swap them during the reinstall so you only pay for one mobilization. Call (970) 286-3417 and we'll coordinate timing directly with your roofer.
